collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall register the dog... No person shall use a dog tag upon a dog other than the dog for which the tag was issued.
dog_limit: Not more than three dogs shall be kept at any residence within the boundaries of the Municipality.
notes: URL: https://faraday.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Dog-By-Law-2016.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw with a 3-dog limit. No specific exemptions or definitions for LGDs or farm dogs.

lgd_definition: “livestock guardian dog” – means a dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals to protect them while repelling predators and is used exclusively for that purpose;
herding_definition: “herding dog” – means a dog that has been trained and is actively being used in a bona fide farming operation for the purposed controlling of livestock on the farm;
collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog or cat must purchase a tag on or before January 1st each year.
dog_limit: There is no limit on the number of dogs and cats that a person can have in the Town of Fort Frances, provided adequate care can be given.
notes: URL: https://www.fortfrances.ca/sites/default/files/5017_animal_control.pdf. The bylaw explicitly defines both Livestock Guardian Dogs and Herding Dogs. The municipality does not place a numerical limit on the number of dogs a person can own.

lgd_definition: “Working Dog” shall mean a dog trained to aid in herding or protecting livestock or a dog trained for and used for dog sledding.
collar_tag_req: On payment of the license fee the owner shall be provided with a dog tag bearing a serial number and the year for which the tag is issued for each dog registered and licensed.
dog_limit: The maximum number of dogs per household, except for Service Dogs, Guide Dogs, Working Dogs or Hunting Dogs, shall be restricted to three (3).
notes: URL: https://www.georgianbluffs.ca/media/c1efh0ij/animal-control.pdf. Very farm-friendly bylaw. Working dogs (which includes protecting and herding livestock) are specifically exempted from the 3-dog limit per household and are also exempt from 'running at large' provisions while actively working.

collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog in the Town of Goderich shall... cause such a dog to be licensed... and keep the dog tag affixed to the dog.
dog_limit: Prohibiting the keeping of more than a total of four pets in a dwelling unit – two being dogs.
notes: URL: https://www.goderich.ca/media/lzho13vl/63-2017-animal-control-by-law-accessible.pdf. Standard urban animal control bylaw with a strict pet limit. No farm dog or LGD provisions.

BYLAW NOT FOUND. The Town of Erin has an active 'Dog Control and Kennel By-law' (By-law 15-57), but the full text of the document is not publicly accessible online to extract the specific definitions or LGD provisions.

bylaw_name: Control and Licensing of Dogs By-Law
collar_tag_req: Upon payment of the applicable license fee, the owner shall be furnished with a dog tag bearing a serial number.
dog_limit: No dog owner shall possess any more than 3 dogs at one time in a single dwelling unit. Dog kennels are prohibited entirely.
notes: URL: https://www.gorebay.ca/media/fxvpgp2u/control-and-licensing-of-dogs-by-law.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw. Service dogs are expressly exempt from the licensing fee, but no exemptions exist for working or farm dogs.

collar_tag_req: Every owner or harbourer of a Dog shall obtain a tag and keep it securely fixed on his Dog.
dog_limit: No person shall own, keep or harbour more than three (3) dogs per location. However, an amendment (By-Law 28-2018) specifies that more than three (3) dogs per location may be kept on land outside of a Built-up Area.
notes: URL: https://www.greatermadawaska.com/media/wkkpanrb/28-2018-to-amend-animal-control-by-law.pdf. While it lacks explicit LGD definitions, the by-law is very rural-friendly by exempting non-built-up areas (rural/agricultural properties) from the 3-dog limit.

collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall ensure that a lost, damaged or destroyed identification tag is replaced immediately.
dog_limit: No owner shall keep or permit to be kept more than three (3) dogs in a residential area. On all other premises, no owner shall keep more than five (5) dogs.
notes: URL: https://www.haldimandcounty.ca/government-administration/by-laws-and-policies/by-law-directory/animal-control-by-law/. Dog limits are increased to 5 for non-residential properties (which includes agricultural), offering some flexibility for farms.

collar_tag_req: No person shall board a dog that does not have a current valid licence, registration or tag from the Town or from another municipality.
dog_limit: No person shall keep, either on a temporary or permanent basis, more than four (4) domestic animals with a maximum of two (2) dogs in any residential dwelling unit.
notes: URL: https://www.hawkesbury.ca/uploads/documents/R%C3%A9glements-municipaux/BY-LAW-N%C2%B0-36-2020-CONSOLIDATED-2024-Animal-Control.pdf. Standard urban animal control bylaw with a strict limit of 2 dogs per residential dwelling unit. No LGD or farm dog exemptions found.

collar_tag_req: All dog owners must obtain an annual dog license before the dog is three months old and the license tag must be attached to the dog's collar.
dog_limit: A maximum of 4 domestic animals per household in urban areas.
notes: URL: https://www.hamilton.ca/sites/default/files/2022-07/12-031-officeconsolidation-jun16-22.pdf. The Responsible Animal Ownership By-Law regulates pets in Hamilton. Although there are no specific definitions for LGDs, Section 7.12 regulates unreasonable animal noise (barking) but explicitly states: 'This section does not apply to noise from an animal on a farm.' (As amended by By-law 18-008).
